title: Midcycle course correction & town rituals — company sync proposal (v0.2)
content:
Purpose:

This doc proposes a focused midcycle course-correction for company-level priorities and a lightweight all-hands / town ritual that signals (1) what’s changing in our OKR commitments, (2) immediate org-level actions to protect delivery, and (3) clear owner-level next steps to get us back on trajectory before quarter close.

Context summary (short):
- Midway through the quarter we are seeing three pressure points: sustained latency regressions on a small subset of hosted models, slower-than-expected adoption of Redwood Dedicated beta by mid-market customers, and a rising backlog of audit/compliance requests for Private deployments.
- Cumulative progress against company OKRs is ~55% of expected midcycle milestone completion; variance concentrated in Performance & Dedicated revenue streams.
- Feedback from last leadership standup: teams want explicit trade guidance rather than ambiguous prioritization during the rest of the quarter.

Principles for this course correction:
1) Bias for clarity and owner accountability over aspirational scope.
2) Preserve customer-facing SLAs and retain product availability at the cost of non-essential internal polish.
3) Protect runway on Dedicated GTM motions that have legal/security gating.
4) Timebox scope changes to this midcycle window only; do not rewrite longer-term strategy.

Proposed company-level adjustments (summary):
- OKR A (Serving Reliability): Move from target P95 latency <= 320ms to two-track target: P95<=320ms for Tier-1 models (hosted catalog top-10) + P95<=520ms for Tier-2 models. Rationale: focus infrastructure effort and SRE headcount on high-volume models.
- OKR B (Revenue — Dedicated): Reframe Q commit to: 60% of Dedicated pipeline value to be pipeline-validated with legal/compliance gating cleared (previous target tied to closed bookings). This recognizes gating delays and prioritizes unblock work.
- OKR C (Private / Compliance): Add a new sub-key result: complete audit remediation checklist for top three enterprise pilots and publish customer-facing readiness checklist.

Leading indicators & success metrics (what we track this sprint):
- # of Tier-1 models with confirmed kernel optimizations deployed (target 6/10 within 3 weeks).
- Number of Dedicated contracts where KYC/KMS integration is greenlit (target 4 pilots moved to legal-ready).
- Audit remediation items closed (target 80% of top-3 pilot items).
- Rolling NPS signal for Dedicated pilot customers (qualitative check-in: 2-week cadence).

Executive update talking points (1-minute bullets for CEO/CTO):
- Quick status: midcycle adjustment to concentrate SRE, infra, and applied-ML resources on Tier-1 hosted models and Dedicated legal gating.
- Why: disproportionate impact of a few models and gating on revenue and ops noise.
- Ask: temporary reallocation of 8 engineer-weeks and 2 SRE on-call rotations to Tier-1 model work; leadership sign-off to adjust KR thresholds.

All-hands / Town ritual proposal (single 45-minute session + optional breakouts):
- Title: "Midcycle: Focus & Fix"
- Overall goal: align all teams on the reprioritized focus, highlight visible mitigations, and commit owners with due dates.
- Format (45m):
  * 0–5m: Quick framing from CEO (what changed and why).
  * 5–15m: CTO/Head of Serving runtime 90-second model-level status for top 5 models (what’s broken, who’s on it).
  * 15–25m: Head of Revenue/Head of Dedicated — short update on pipeline gating and customer impact.
  * 25–35m: Company-ops: timeline and concrete allocations (which teams will be temporarily repurposed; SAFETY net and SLA expectations).
  * 35–45m: Live decision board: 3 binary decisions that leadership must sign-off on (KR threshold changes, temporary hiring freeze exceptions, external customer comms template).
- Post-town rituals: 1) Publish a short ‘what we decided’ snippet to all staff + customers; 2) Auto-create the action tracker with owners and ETA per leader; 3) Weekly 20-minute check-ins for the remainder of the quarter on Friday mornings.

Communications plan (external + internal):
- Internal: One-pager summary + FAQ in Confluence within 24 hours; pinned Slack thread in #company-ops with action tracker; skip-theater comms for teams not impacted.
- External: Customer-facing email to Dedicated pilots if gating affects delivery timelines — templated and approved by legal (target send within 72 hours if needed).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Temporary concentration might delay features that influence PLG metrics. Mitigation: freeze non-blocking UX experiments for 3 weeks; keep essential telemetry live.
- Risk: Teams feel this is mission creep. Mitigation: leaders to publish a 2-week scope box and resume normal cadence immediately after the checkpoint window.
- Risk: Comms fatigue. Mitigation: single concise note + two follow-ups (owner progress, final recap) rather than many fragmented updates.

Decision log (items requiring leadership sign-off at town ritual):
- Approve two-track latency KR for Tier-1/2 models.
- Approve reassignment of 8 engineer-weeks and 2 SRE rotations for 3-week window.
- Approve customer email template for Dedicated pilot delays.

Immediate next steps (owner / due date):
- Draft concise Confluence page + one-pager (Owner: Maya Chen; Due: 2026-02-22).
- CTO to publish model priority list and engineering assignments (Owner: Arjun Patel; Due: 2026-02-24).
- Legal to pre-approve customer comm template (Owner: Lena Novak; Due: 2026-02-25).
- Head of Revenue to brief pilot customers selectively (Owner: Sofia Rodriguez; Due: 2026-02-26).

Open questions / discussion points for leadership:
1) Are we comfortable changing a company-level KR mid-quarter (yes/no)? If yes, what signal do we want to customers?
2) Should we extend the weekly 20-minute check-ins beyond the quarter if progress remains slow?
3) Is a permanent “model triage” rotation needed in future sprints?

Appendix (short):
A. Quick timeline: Week 0 (decision) -> Week 1 (deploy top fixes) -> Week 2 (customer comms + pipeline unblock) -> Week 3 (reassess and restore).
B. Minimal comms template outline attached in Confluence link above.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive: please call out if you prefer less centralization of resource pulls.
- If you are a manager of an engineering pod that will be affected, add a 2-line comment in the Confluence page: impact + earliest availability window.

End of doc.
